title: Dignity Destruction
text: “Itsuki, stop! That’s overkill! There’s no need to go that far with these guys in the first place! It’s bad for your spirit too, so no using that weapon!”

“Oh? Naofumi-san, saying that out of concern for me? Ever the compassionate one, as always—fine, I’ll hold back. But please, finish it off in some satisfying way. Otherwise I just can’t forgive people who did something so selfish. You saw that footage of the demi-humans and beastmen—they think it was justified punishment, you know?”
“Itsuki… you… well, I suppose for people who’d affirm a situation grotesque enough to make even the king recoil, this is the fate they deserve.”
“Yes, even if we kill them, please do it in a way that tramples their dignity.”
“…Wife. Is that Wilhelm’s cue for me to shine here? What was that line just now, the Shield seems troubled.”
Trash asked the queen this while watching the rest of us discuss overwhelming those wretches from a position of absolute strength.
The queen turned her face away and said nothing, hiding her mouth behind her fan.
“Trample their dignity, huh… well, I can’t exactly sympathize with them, but I’m not really into killing either… living on would probably be more painful for them, so let’s at least show some mercy.”
Father seemed to be racking his brains for some good idea.
“That’s insane!?”
The soldiers off to the side let out cries of shock too. They’d gone speechless after their trump card failed to land.
“This is wrong! Impossible!? Don’t tell me it’s defective!?”
“Bu-bu-buhi!? Bu-bu-buhyaaaaaaaaaaa! Buhyaaaaa!”
Some reddish-black pig came charging toward us, but the queen froze it in place with ice magic.

“How insolent! Don’t you dare come running to our side the moment you realize you’ve been deceived. You already had more than enough time and opportunity to think this through. It’s too late for that.”
“The nerve of it, trying to switch sides the moment the wind turns against it—what shamelessness!”
Trash hurled words of contempt at the reddish-black pig, but the queen furrowed her brow and tilted her head at Trash.

“Aultcray? Malty will likely do the very same thing, you know? No, in fact, she’s essentially already done it. That child we captured will probably show us this very same spectacle, so please brace yourself.”
“That’s not true! Wife! Don’t lump that child in with this creature!”
Crocodile Guy watched this scene alongside Éclair with a pained expression.
“I hate to say it, but not being the Shield Hero and all… how should I even weigh in on this?”
“Shion, I understand you have feelings about this. But… this is simply reality. We should focus on what comes next and not worry about the scene unfolding before us.”
“Ah… I’d like to believe that. But I have a feeling the punchline waiting for us later is going to be something appallingly awful.”
This was an episode later recounted almost nostalgically by Father, Crocodile Guy, and Rabbit Guy, noting how there’d been no sense of tension at all.
“Father, Father.”
“What, Motoyasu-kun? I get intensely uneasy whenever you propose something at a time like this.”
“I have a brilliant plan to destroy these fellows’ dignity, satisfying Itsuki in the process, indeed.”
“What an awful thing to say…”
Father gazed off into the distance as if praying for strength, then looked at me.
“Oh? Motoyasu-san has had a flash of inspiration? I’m curious what that might be. How do you plan to finish them off?”

“Leave it to me, I say. As the one who dealt with Takt so thoroughly, I’ve already decided on the method of disposal that would leave these fellows dying in the most humiliating way possible, indeed!”

And with that, I began chanting a spell. That’s right—these fellows had branded Father, the Shield Hero worshipped as a god by demi-humans and beastmen, as the root of all evil and an enemy, rebelled against the queen who cooperated with him, seized the castle, and challenged us to a decisive battle wielding toy-like copy weapons. For such fellows, sending them to the afterlife mercifully—yet while thoroughly crushing their dignity, rather than torture or shipping them off to the Pig King—was clearly the most humiliating option, indeed.
“By the power vested in the Love Hunter, source of all strength, I command thee. Unravel the very fabric of creation once more, and transform the forms of these beings.”
“Al Faery Morph!”

I figured it would be nice if the range covered me, Father, Ren, and even Trash. Trash… seemed to be right on the borderline, might catch, might not. The response was ambiguous, indeed. It had that gray, iffy feeling like it might just fail to take. With a poof, our forms shifted into fairy shapes, indeed. Oh!? Trash got caught too, it seems!
“Nuwah!? What is this!? What’s happened to me!?”
“Aultcray… oh my, so that’s what you look like… this isn’t bad at all.”
“Wife! What exactly are you thinking with that look in your eyes!?”
It seemed Trash turning into a fairy had sparked a different sort of curiosity in the queen.
“Whoa!? Motoyasu! Of all the things to say, this is what you came up with!?”
“Waah!?”

We struck a pose, having become fairies with a little skip. Incidentally, since I hadn’t prepared any clothes for this, they’d all slipped right off. I really needed to bring along some fairy-appropriate outfits for next time, indeed.
“Wh-what!?”
With our transformed appearances, the new pope and the fake Trash’s expressions shifted to even greater shock mixed with something resembling delight.
“So you’ve finally shown your true colors! Impostors posing as heroes, mere beastmen after all—so the Sage King of Wisdom was one too!”
“You misunderstand! Y-you, what have you done to me, Shieeeeeeeld!”
“It wasn’t meeeeeee!?”
I swiftly closed in on the new pope, cleaved his copy weapon in a single stroke, and in one fluid motion drove my spear through him, hoisting him aloft, indeed.
“Do you have time to be chatting leisurely, nyoin?”
This form isn’t our true identity—it’s merely magic I used to change our shapes so that your ends could be as humiliating as possible, nyoin. Our true forms are human, nyoin. Fuhahaha, nyoin.
“Gah…!? Y-you insolent… being struck down by mere beastmen…”

The new pope’s expression grew even more filled with fury and humiliation than before, indeed. That’s right, indeed. Even branding them as impostors, in some corner of their hearts, these fellows still held onto the notion that heroes, being human, were people just like them. By showing them a fairy form resembling that of beastmen, we made them recognize us as the very enemies they despised. Being killed by that hated beastman—that was the most humiliating fate imaginable for them, indeed.
“Well then, farewell, nyoin. Burst Lance X!”
“You insolent—!”
Boom! I sent the new pope flying spectacularly.
“Fuhahahaha… this is the true other form of the gods, nyoin. The very deities you worship possess this exact form, nyoin.”
“You’re no god, nothing of the sort! Dieeeeeeeeeee!”

The fake Trash shed his disguise and lunged forward, driven purely by emotion, indeed. But he charged not at me, but at Father, indeed. What’s more, the Three Heroes Church soldiers from the sidelines came swarming in too, indeed.
“Enemy of the gods, Shield Herooooooooo! Now that you’ve shown your true colors, we’ll kill you!”
“Hey, Theo! Hand over the Shield Hero!”
“No way I’m doing that! Like I’d ever hand him over to you! Iwatani-sama is under my protection!”
“Hold on, Theo? Shion?”

The moment I’d taken my eyes off them, Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy—both looking somewhat unhinged—seemed to be fighting over Father. Itsuki, meanwhile, had apparently been tossed aside like garbage. He was watching the commotion with an amused grin, indeed.
“Well then, allow me to clear the path for you.”
Stomp, stomp—I went about headshotting the swarming soldiers one by one, indeed.
“Shion, ‘hand him over’ is—hey! Calm down! What’s gotten into you!?”
Éclair, sensing something off about Crocodile Guy—who’d lost himself trying to wrestle Father away from Rabbit Guy—raised her voice in alarm.
“Haaaaaaaah!”
“Out of my way!”
“Step aside!”
Bam! Crocodile Guy sent the body double disguised as Trash flying with a swipe of his tail, and Rabbit Guy’s graceful kick exploded into it, sending it flying straight toward me.
“Welcome, nyoin.”
Since it was flying at me anyway, I simply held my spear steady, and with a squelch, it drove itself deep through the body.
